rescope_hatch_feasibility.candidate_method: Olkin & Finn (1995, Psychological Bulletin 117:330-333) asymptotic-normal variance formula for a single-model R^2: Var(R^2) ~= 4*R^2*(1-R^2)^2*(n-k-1)^2 / ((n^2-1)*(n+3)), combined naively (assuming independence) into a CI for the R^2 difference B3-B4. Chosen because it is the only candidate that needs ONLY already-published aggregate numbers (R^2, n, k) and no per-row or per-polymer arrays.
rescope_hatch_feasibility.conclusion: No analytically sound, non-fabricated small-sample interval for R2(B3)-R2(B4) over the 13 independent test polymers is derivable from the currently-published aggregate KPI fields alone. Every candidate shortcut either (a) silently assumes row-level independence the pre-registered method exists to avoid, (b) requires per-cluster values that are not published and cannot be manufactured without re-consuming the quarantined CSV, or (c) requires a parameter count that was never recorded for the ML model. Computing and reporting any of these numbers as the item's CI would itself be a fabricated attack: a number chosen to look like it satisfies the acceptance criterion without the statistical grounding the criterion requires. The re-scope hatch is therefore evaluated and NOT invoked this fire.

problem_1_row_count_ignores_clustering.description: The formula's n means independent observations. The KPI's own population note states the 194 test rows come from only 13 unique novel test polymers -- i.e. n_eff <= 13, not 194. Using n=194 (the only row-level count actually published) silently assumes independence the pre-registered cluster bootstrap exists specifically to NOT assume. This is the identical anti-conservative failure mode already documented against this module: amphora-viscosity-score/evidence/phase0/kpis/N=60-scaffold Monte Carlo finding (repeated-scaffold resampling REFUTED a single-seed coverage claim that a naive i.i.d.-row treatment had passed).

problem_2_cluster_count_substitution_is_.description: Substituting n=13 (cluster count) for n in the same row-level formula is not a valid re-derivation -- the formula's r2/(1-r2)^2 terms were still computed from the 194-row pooled residuals, not from 13 independent per-polymer R^2 values. Relabeling n without recomputing the statistic from actual per-cluster quantities produces a number with no defensible sampling-distribution interpretation -- it is not a valid cluster-robust SE, just a smaller number obtained by putting a smaller n into a formula that was never derived for a plug-in n substitution of this kind.
problem_2_cluster_count_substitution_is_.verdict: NOT A VALID CLUSTER-ROBUST BOUND -- included only to show the substitution is computable, not that it is meaningful.

problem_3_b4_parameter_count_undefined.description: The formula also needs k, the number of fitted parameters, to compute degrees of freedom n-k-1. The KPI's own artifact field records B4's n_fitted_parameters as the string 'many (histogram GBM leaves)', not an integer. There is no principled small integer to substitute; HistGBM's effective parameter count is dataset- and hyperparameter-dependent and was never persisted. At n_clusters=13 almost any realistic k for a boosted-tree model exceeds n-1, making n-k-1 <= 0 and the formula literally undefined (returns None above).

problem_4_r2_vs_pearson_r2_divergence.description: A simpler Fisher-z-on-pearson_r shortcut is also unsound here: for B4, pearson_r^2 (0.6403) exceeds the reported R^2 (0.4536) by 0.1868. R^2 = 1 - SSE/SST penalizes prediction bias/miscalibration in addition to decorrelation; pearson_r^2 does not. This module's own prior finding (amphora-viscosity-score-score-eyring-apriori: Eyring 23.8% LOO REFUTED) already documents ML predictions on held-out novel chemistry drifting out of calibration even while remaining correlated. A correlation-based shortcut would understate B4's true generalization gap and bias the resulting interval toward the physics-wins conclusion for the wrong reason.
